Hi Elena —

Thanks for the heads-up over the demo request form. We'd like to run a focused architecture deep-dive next week so we can map Redwood's evidence artifacts to MedLoop's SOC 2 controls and surface any gaps early. Proposed 60–75 minute agenda:

- 5m: introductions and goals
- 20m: high-level architecture (networking, VPC, region failover, KMS key management)
- 20m: evidence mapping (audit logs, retention, SIEM integrations)
- 15m: SSO and provisioning (SCIM, SAML metadata, role mapping)
- 10m: open questions, next steps / mutual action plan

Available slots (PST):
- Tues 2026-11-30 10:00–11:15
- Wed 2026-12-01 09:00–10:15
- Wed 2026-12-01 14:00–15:15

I've attached a short Excel with the initial evidence request set (medloop_evidence_request_v1.xlsx) so you can skim before the call. If you prefer a later time or need an earlier window, let us know and we'll try to accommodate. Please loop in any of your security architects — we'll make this as technical as you need.

Best,

Vivek Kulkarni

Thanks everyone — confirmed for Thu 2026-12-02 08:00–09:30 PST (calendar invite sent). Quick answers so procurement has something to cite before the call:

- Audit log residency: Redwood can configure log routing so customer audit logs remain in the chosen region (we support region-bound retention buckets). Where customers use our hosted analytics we do store telemetry in our US region by default; for Private/Dedicated deployments we operate with region-local storage. We'll include a short section in the agenda PDF clarifying options.

- KMS rotation: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) and can integrate with AWS KMS via external key config; rotation is handled by your KMS policy. For our managed key paths, we rotate CMKs on a 90-day cadence and can provide rotation logs as part of evidence.

Attached: redwood_arch_agenda_v2.pdf (agenda + evidence map). Looking forward to the session — Vivek, Marissa, and Neha will be there.

Best,
Vivek
